page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.sgn7i-vws-m4.2xlarge is a virtualized server instance running on the KVM hypervisor. It is built on the x86_64 architecture and features an Intel Xeon 8369B processor with a base frequency of 2.9 GHz. The hardware configuration includes 8 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 4 physical cores with hyper-threading, 31.0 GB of system memory, and a 48 MB L3 cache. Graphics and parallel computing acceleration are provided by a fractional NVIDIA A10 GPU slice (0.1667 of a full GPU) with 4 GB of dedicated VRAM. This instance does not include local storage and relies on external block storage, while baseline network bandwidth is rated at 3 Gbps.

In benchmark evaluations, the instance demonstrates mid-tier performance characteristics. It achieves a stress-ng single-core CPU score of 1911.28 and a multi-core score of 15139.35. Memory performance tests show a read-only small block bandwidth of 843.39 GB/sec and a write large block bandwidth of 44.65 GB/sec. For specialized rendering and processing, the instance records a Geekbench ray tracing score of 13213.0 and an image processing score of 8323.0. Database operations are supported by a Redis SET throughput of 16.98 million operations per second and a Passmark database score of 4093.14.

The primary architectural tradeoff of this instance lies in its fractional GPU allocation. Provisioning a 0.1667 slice of an NVIDIA A10 GPU offers a highly resource-dense and qualitatively cost-efficient profile for workloads that require hardware acceleration but cannot utilize a full GPU. However, this configuration imposes strict limits on model sizes and parallel execution. While the instance handles small-scale LLM inference efficiently, achieving 198.84 tokens/sec for text generation on a 135M model, performance drops to a weak 8.13 tokens/sec on a medium 7B model, and 70B models cannot be loaded due to the 4 GB VRAM limit.

This instance is best suited for entry-level GPU-accelerated applications, virtual workstations, lightweight machine learning inference using small models, image processing pipelines, and general-purpose workloads requiring moderate parallel compute capabilities.
